analysis: Shina ráati retains initial root accent and final i. Palula feminine raát denotes a counted night-and-day period and has i-declension plural reetí; Strand Phal-r.html40–41 explicitly derives it from rā́tri10702. Ordinary Palula night is a separate fixed a-declension róot/róota, which Strand assigns to neuter rātra10700. The aa/ee i-declension screen now supplies an independently defined modern class for raát/reetí: 73 comparable citation/inflection form pairs, representing66 lexemes, all have late citation accent and final inflectional i accent. This explains its synchronic class membership without proving exactly when or how its inherited accent was reassigned. Kalkoti ordinary ràat is better compared semantically with róot; its Low still lacks an explanation from Palula aspiration alone.
